# SECLEAF Q2 CTF 2026 Force-push-wont-save-you — Writeup.

Vanessa krystal

2 min read

·

May 25, 2026

--

Listen

Share

## Challenge Description

> A developer force-pushed several times before the repository was archived.
> We suspect sensitive data may still exist somewhere in the project history.
> Some objects may no longer be referenced.

Flag format: `SecLeaf{}`

## Initial Analysis

The challenge description immediately suggested a Git forensics challenge involving:

  * rewritten Git history,
  * force-pushes,
  * dangling commits,
  * unreachable Git objects.

The phrase:

> “Some objects may no longer be referenced”

was the biggest clue because Git often retains deleted commits and blobs internally even after a force push.

After extracting the archive, I inspected the contents of the repository.
    
    unzip challenge.zip
    cd force-push-wont-save-you

Listing files showed a hidden `.git` directory was included.
    
    ls -la

## Checking Git History

The first step was reviewing the available commit history.
    
    git log --oneline --all

Several suspicious commit messages appeared, including references to temporary files and cleanup operations.

Example:
    
    remove sensitive data
    cleanup before push
    temporary env backup

This strongly suggested secrets may have existed in earlier commits.

## Inspecting Reflogs

Even after force-pushing, Git reflogs can preserve references to previous states.

I checked all reflogs using:
    
    git reflog --all

This revealed references to commits that were no longer visible in the normal branch history.

One particularly suspicious entry was:
    
    backup before rewrite

At this point it became clear that the developer had attempted to rewrite history but Git still retained older objects.

## Recovering Unreachable Objects

To identify hidden Git objects, I used:
    
    git fsck --full --no-reflogs --unreachable --lost-found

The command reported several unreachable objects:
    
    unreachable commit a197682...
    unreachable blob 24dab13...
    unreachable blob 6d7e0a0...

This confirmed that deleted Git objects still existed inside the repository database.

## Inspecting Hidden Blobs

I then examined the unreachable blobs directly.
    
    git show 24dab13
    git show 6d7e0a0

Some blobs contained fake or decoy flags such as:
    
    SecLeaf{still_fake}
    SecLeaf{fake_dangling_flag}

This indicated the challenge intentionally included misleading artifacts.

## Finding the Real Flag

Next, I searched through the entire repository history for any occurrence of the flag format.
    
    git grep "SecLeaf" $(git rev-list --all)

This revealed a hidden environment file containing:

This revealed a hidden environment file containing:
    
    FLAG=SecLeaf{history_was_the_trap}

This was the actual challenge flag.

## Final Flag
    
    SecLeaf{history_was_the_trap}

# SecLeaf Q2 CTF 2026

SecLeaf.

📅 16 May 2026 🌐 Online 🏷️ Free

## 🚀 About the Event

SecLeaf CTF is a high octane, 24 hour public Jeopardy style Capture The Flag competition. It is meticulously designed to simulate real-world cybersecurity scenarios, pushing participants to solve practical challenges that mirror industry threats. Whether you are a beginner looking to learn or an advanced hacker ready to dominate the leaderboard, this event serves as a premier training ground for the global cybersecurity community.

* * *

## 📊 Event Details

  * Organizer: SecLeaf.
  * Format: 100% Online (Jeopardy-style).
  * Categories: Web, Crypto, Forensics, OSINT, and Misc.
  * Access: Public CTF (Open to all levels).
  * Flag Format: `SecLeaf{...}` (Case-sensitive).

## 📅 Critical Dates

  * Event Window: 23rd May – 24th May, 2026.
  * Duration: 24 Hours (Non-stop).
  * Operational Note: The clock is absolute; no extensions or exceptions will be granted.

## 🎁 Prizes & Rewards

  * Current Prize Pool: $14,150 (Note: This value is subject to increase as more sponsors are added).
  * Winner Verification: The Top 3 Teams are required to submit a detailed technical write-up within 24 hours of the event ending to prove their methodology and claim rewards.

## ⚖️ Mission Protocol (Rules of Engagement)

  * Anti-Cheating: Flag sharing, exploiting unintended platform vulnerabilities, or attacking the infrastructure results in immediate disqualification.
  * Team Ethics: Collaboration is strictly limited to within your own team. Disrupting other teams is a bannable offense.
  * Infrastructure: No DoS/DDoS or brute-forcing the CTF platform. Only interact with systems explicitly provided for challenges.
  * AI Usage Policy: AI is allowed for concept understanding and syntax assistance. However, feeding entire challenge descriptions to an AI for direct solutions or using automated AI solving pipelines is strictly prohibited.

## 🧠 The CTF Challenge

  * The Hunt: Solve challenges ranging from beginner to expert difficulty to find the hidden “flags.”
  * The Tools: Standard legal security tools (Nmap, Burp Suite, Wireshark, Ghidra) are permitted unless a specific challenge states otherwise.
  * The Goal: Accumulate points by submitting flags exactly as formatted. In the event of a points tie, the team that reached the score first wins.

## 📝 How to Enter

  * Step 1: Register your team (Beginner to Advanced levels welcome).
  * Step 2: Prepare your environment (Kali Linux/Parrot OS recommended).
  * Step 3: Monitor the official SecLeaf channels for the start signal on May 23rd.
  * Step 4: Ensure you are ready to document your steps, especially if you are aiming for a Top 3 finish.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
